title: Étale maps of E∞-rings and étale maps of spectral Deligne-Mumford stacks
statement_scope: Whole Theorem 1.2.1: let φ: A → B be a map of E∞-rings. Then φ is étale if and only if the induced map Spec B → Spec A is an étale map of nonconnective spectral Deligne-Mumford stacks.

proof_spans.label: Proof of Theorem 1.2.1, with Lemmas 1.2.3-1.2.12 used in the proof

Lemma 1.2.12 (étale descent along faithfully flat maps)

standard_prerequisites: Definition of étale morphism of spectrally ringed ∞-topoi (Section 1.2, author PDF p. 11).
Structure theory of étale morphisms of E∞-rings, Proposition VII.8.10.
Theorem A.7.5.0.6 and Theorem A.7.5.4.2 on lifting étale algebras and isomorphisms of π0.
Corollary A.7.5.4.5 on étaleness after faithfully flat base change.
Lemma 1.2.5, Proposition 1.2.7, Proposition 1.2.8, and Lemma 1.2.12 (author PDF pp. 12-15).
difficulty_reason: Rule author-work-bearing-core-v1-20261114: H3 because the complete proof at author PDF pp. 11-15 supplies the main research-bearing comparison of the subsection, not a citation assembly: it reduces to discrete A, bounds eφ and inducts on it, uses Lemma 1.2.5, Lemma 1.2.12 and étale descent along a faithfully flat cover, reduces to the case of a section, applies Proposition 1.2.7 and Proposition 1.2.8 to split off a clopen Spec A summand, and then handles the general nonconnective case via Theorem A.7.5.0.6 and Theorem A.7.5.4.2. This is the substantive theorem of section 1.2.

difficulty_evidence.bearing_core: Reduction of the étale comparison to discrete A, induction on eφ, faithfully flat descent, section/clopen decomposition, and nonconnective lifting.
